- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% for 5–10 days.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment to dampen forecast volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 1–2% for 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may misread sentiment as bullish; reduce forecast by 2–4% for 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is low and price is rising, model may misread as bullish; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 5–10 days.
- Model often underestimates price volatility in low-sentiment periods; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for 3–7 days if sentiment <0.4.
